Final Year Project · 2026

An Autoencoder Host-Based Intrusion Detection System Trained on Benign Network Flow Behavioral Features

A host-based IDS that learns what normal encrypted traffic looks like from flow behavior, and raises an alert when that behavior changes.

ResearchersNelson MivuleErecho Jonathan
SupervisorMr. Senfuka Huzaifah
InstitutionUTAMUSchool of Computing and Engineering
ScapyTensorFlow / KerasFastAPI · SQLitePySide6

02 — Motivation

Why behavior, not content

1
Encryption is the norm
HTTPS, TLS and VPNs protect most traffic on the internet today.
→
2
Encryption also hides threats
With sophisticated tools, attackers embed malicious traffic inside normal traffic. This changes its behavior: shape, size, volume and timing.
→
3
Learn normal, alert on change
The autoencoder learns normal flow behavior and generates an alert when that behavior shifts.
Key idea: content is hidden, but the behavior of the flow is not.

03 — Problem & Gap

Where current tools fall short

Problem: about 95% of web traffic is encrypted, so payload-based inspection cannot see inside it.
ApproachLimitationAE-HIDS
Deep packet inspection · Snort, SuricataNeeds readable payloads; misses zero-daysUses flow behavior; no decryption
Manual scripting · ZeekHand-written rules; heavy upkeepAutoencoder learns the baseline itself
Host monitoring · OSSECLog-based; blind to encrypted flowsReads host flow metadata directly
Contribution: analyzing encrypted traffic with flow behavioral features to generate alerts. It does not claim to solve every attack.

05 — System Architecture & Operation

Four tiers, one operational chain

1
Capture
Scapy reads raw host packets
2
Group
5-tuple flows, scored after 5+ packets
3
Extract
22 behavioral features, headers only
4
Encode, decode
22→16→8→4→8→16→22
5
Measure
MSE between input and rebuilt output
6
Decide
Above 0.5: alert. Otherwise: normal

06 — Autoencoder

Learn normal, flag what changes

1 · Train on normal
Benign flows only. No attack is ever seen in training.
2 · Reconstruct
Normal flows rebuild well. Changed behavior rebuilds badly.
3 · Compare
Reconstruction error above the 0.5 threshold raises an alert.
MSE below 0.5
Flagged as normal traffic.
MSE above 0.5
Alert sent to the dashboard and logged.

07 — Training & Evaluation

Training results

Training
  • Benign flows only
  • 100 epochs, 387 s, CPU only
  • No over-fitting seen
  • Scoring 0.661 ms/flow, 1,965 flows/s
At threshold 0.5
  • ROC-AUC 0.957
  • False alarms 923 of 98,345 (0.94%)
  • Detected 34,559 attacks, missed 173,979

08 — Testing & Validation

Tested across host layers, not just the GUI

Network · Transport
Unit
Scapy capture, 5-tuple flows and 22-feature vectors; encoder, decoder and MSE in isolation.
Host · Services
Integration
An anomalous flow over the threshold is logged in SQLite and shown in the dashboard.
End to end
System
Full pipeline from packet sniffing to inference, storage and visualization.
Speed & load
Performance
Inference latency, ingestion throughput and database writes under continuous traffic.
Analyst workflows
User acceptance
Analysts set thresholds, review per-feature errors, mark false positives and export reports.
Offline detection test: held-out CIC-IDS2017 flows the model never saw in training.

10 — Conclusion

From manual operation to learned, visible monitoring

Before
Unverified, manual operation
Encrypted traffic hidden from content inspection; signatures and hand-written scripts.
This project
Learned, standardized, visible
An autoencoder that adapts to normal behavior, with runtime monitoring on the host.
Evidence
  • Working pipeline from capture to dashboard
  • ROC-AUC 0.957, 0.94% false alarms
  • 0.661 ms per flow on a CPU-only laptop
Next steps
  • Lower thresholds and per-attack recall
  • Test on live and encrypted-port attacks
